                    <div class="title-desc-wrapper has-main-image">
                      <div class="title-desc-inner" data-collection-id="58c76e9137c581e1410a1387" data-edit-main-image="Background">
                        <div class="page-title-wrapper"><h1 class="page-title" data-content-field="title">Sakalava Kitespot</h1></div>
                        <br> 
                        <div class="page-desc" data-content-field="description"><p>Perfection is in Sakalava Bay</p></div>
                      </div>
                    </div>
                  </div>
          <section id="content-wrapper">
            <div class="content">
              <div class="content-inner" data-content-field="main-content">
                <div class="sqs-layout sqs-grid-12 columns-12" data-type="page" data-updated-on="1735616611918" id="page-58c76e9137c581e1410a1387"><div class="row sqs-row"><div class="col sqs-col-12 span-12"><div class="row sqs-row"><div class="col sqs-col-6 span-6"><div class="sqs-block html-block sqs-block-html" data-block-type="2" data-sqsp-block="text" id="block-yui_3_17_2_51_1489458216313_12711"><div class="sqs-block-content">
<div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content>
  <h2 style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Sakalava Bay spot FOR KITESURF, WINDSURF, KITEFOIL, WINGFOIL</h2><h1 style="white-space:pre-wrap;">kitesurfing, WINGFOILING &amp; WINDSURFING IN madagascar</h1><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">In Sakalava Bay the wind blows everyday from morning to dusk, 9 months in a row from mid-March to late December!&nbsp;The kitespot is safe very safe making it the perfect <a href="/kiteschool">spot for learning.</a> <br>The bay allies incredible flat and waves on the reef, which makes Sakalava an all-in-one spot for every practices.<br>Sakalava bay is also very safe, this is the perfect spot for <a href="/kiteschool">beginners</a> !</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"><strong>Flat water and waves</strong><br>KiteParadise is located right on the kite and windsurf spot with perfect flat water just in front of your room.&nbsp;If you prefer to kitesurf or windsurf on waves, you can catch some surf behind the reef.&nbsp;The waves average 2m and break only 500m from the shore. Check out the map with Zones below.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"><strong>Kitefoil and Wingfoil</strong></p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Sakalava Bay is also very good if you want to practice foil (<strong>kitefoil</strong> / <strong>wingfoil</strong>). You can go around the high tide which gives you roughly 4 or 5 hours per day around the high tide (min 40cm/ max 300cm).<br>If you are seeking lighter wind, you have to avoid the period between June and September.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"><strong>Wind conditions<br></strong>Wind direction in Sakalava Bay is side/side-on.<br>Kitesurfing and Windsurfing season in Northern Madagascar runs from mid March to mid December and it peaks between June and September when the wind is strongest.&nbsp;</p><ul data-rte-list="default"><li><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Late March to late April - 15 to&nbsp;25 knots - kites from 9m to&nbsp;14 m</p></li></ul><ul data-rte-list="default"><li><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">May and June - 20 to&nbsp;30 knots - kites from 7m à&nbsp;12 m.</p></li><li><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">July to September - 25 to&nbsp;35 knots - kites from 5m to&nbsp;10m.</p></li><li><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">October - 20 to&nbsp;30 knots - kites from 7m to&nbsp;12m.</p></li><li><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">November until late December - 15 to&nbsp;25 knots - kite from 7m to&nbsp;14m.</p></li></ul><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"><strong>Temperatures</strong><br>Bikini and boardshorts weather! Madagascar and Sakalava bay are fairly hot all year round.&nbsp;Water temperature is usually about 28° Celsius but it can drop down to 23° in July and August so bring a shorty just in case.</p>
</div>

</div></div></div><div class="col sqs-col-6 span-6"><div class="sqs-block html-block sqs-block-html" data-block-type="2" data-sqsp-block="text" id="block-yui_3_17_2_56_1489458216313_210608"><div class="sqs-block-content">
<div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content>
  <h2 style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Zone A</h2><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">At low tide, you'll see a 200m long magnificent sand bank that stretches from the beach to the small island. Thanks to the perpendicular sand bank, Zone A becomes a very flat off-wind area with absolutely no danger since you drift to the beach.</p><h2 style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Zone B</h2><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">At low tide, zone B is a terrific flat mirror area with the steadiest wind in the bay. Kite schools only operate next to the shore, leaving &nbsp;a huge playing area for all other kiters.</p><h2 style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Zone C</h2><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">At medium and high tides, this becomes the area where all wave lovers meet. Waves are usually 1.5m but they can go much higher when the swell is strong.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p><h2 style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Zone D</h2><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">This zone is really flat at low tide but the direction of the wind,&nbsp;combined with the proximity of the mangrove,&nbsp;causes a lot of turbulence in the whole area.</p>
</div>

                overflow: hidden;-webkit-mask-image: -webkit-radial-gradient(white, black);
              "
